ws1_collision.method: exact-identifier match (word boundaries) against builtins (bn_ table, 47), REPL commands (6), keywords (kw_ table, 34), library functions (306), lang/*.lang Latin tokens (54), example identifiers (code only: comments and string literals stripped; 493 identifiers); run on v290 and on current main with identical results
ws1_collision.note_kuru: kuru is already a keyword (kw_kuru, KW_KURU equ 29, 'kuru = do (imperative Sanskrit, for do-while)') and therefore already in the lang packs as that keyword's Sanskrit form; as a MESSAGE word (replacing Hindi karo in one error string) it is not a code collision (message text is not parsed) and the meaning agrees (karo = do, kuru = do); it is not a new name and should be struck from the 'new names' list
ws1_collision.repl_duplication: exit/quit/help already have Sanskrit REPL commands (nirgat, sahayata); adding tyaj/saha creates two Sanskrit words per command without stating what happens to nirgat/sahayata

to_deletion.replacement_note_wrong: the brief says to->prati, but to is the old spelling of the loop-bound keyword tak (kw_to_str db 'tak' in the r4_old_kw table); prati is the return alias, unrelated to loop bounds; the replacement note must say tak, not prati

ws2_sanskrit.bodies_probed: peek=30 (top, no removal); pop=30 with len 3->2 (returns the value); empty=0 then 1 after clear; clear -> len 0, empty 1; enqueue 1,2,3 -> len 3, peek 3 (back, not front); dequeue=1 with len 3->2, peek still 3 (removes the FIRST element, keeps the rest); pankti_len('abc')=0 because pankti_len takes a mala, not a string (BN comment: array length for declared arrays; R23: slice length); char_lower(65)=97, char_upper(97)=65; char_from(66)=an address (handler: pointer to a char in a temp buffer; likha prints it as an address, the #5 trap shape); lkhb(7)='7' with no newline and no point; sankhya_dot from doc + comment: two-argument vector dot product via dpps (not a decimal point)

meaning_flags.akshar_tas: WRONG + fragment — akshar + tas parses as 'from a character' (the suffix attaches to akshar), but char_from(code) yields a character FROM A CODE; direction reversed; tas alone is a suffix, not a word
meaning_flags.kosh_muc: WRONG by R179's own rule — dequeue removes the first element and keeps the rest (probed); it releases nothing; muc is wrong, hri or apanay is right
meaning_flags.likha_bindu: WRONG — bindu (point/dot) unexplained: lkhb prints a number without a newline (probed: '7', no point); the distinguishing feature is no-newline, which bindu does not name
meaning_flags.saha: WRONG + truncation — saha = 'with', not 'help'; the existing Sanskrit help is sahayata (already a REPL command); help->saha truncates sahayata to saha, the paripurna->purn violation
meaning_flags.smaran_kriti: VAGUE + inconsistent — kriti = making/doing, not specifically copying; the project already has a copy word, pratilip (vartani_pratilip, string copy); the consistent name is smaran_pratilip

ws2_sanskrit.passes: asti (is/exists) for ==, nasti (is-not) for !=; truti (fault) for Error, patra (file, already used in messages) for file, rekha (line) for line, kuru (do, agrees with the keyword) for karo; kosh_kship (throw in) for push, kosh_hri (take away) for pop, kosh_gan (count) for len, kosh_iksh (see) for peek, kosh_rikt (empty) for empty, kosh_shodh (cleanse) for clear, kosh_yuj (join) for enqueue, pankti_gan (row-count) for array length, vartani_yoj (join) for cat, likha_rup (form) for fmt, sankhya_bindu (dot) for dot product (neither old nor new name says 'product'; full term would be sankhya_bindu_gunana), akshar_laghu (small) for lower, akshar_guru (great) for upper, jala_bandh/shru/grah (bind/hear/take) for netbind/listen/accept, tyaj (abandon) for exit/quit (meaning apt; root, see systematic note)
ws2_sanskrit.systematic_roots: 13 of 30 are bare roots or a suffix, not complete words: kship, hri, gan, iksh, yuj, muc, shodh, tyaj, bandh, shru, grah, yoj, tas; strictly a root is not a pada (word) until inflected, so under R178's 'complete word or compound, never a fragment' constraint these need their full forms (kshepa, harana, ganana, ikshana, yojana, mocana, shodhana, tyaga, bandha, shravana, grahana, yojana) or an explicit owner decision that roots are accepted (precedent: the project already has a bare-root keyword, yoj); the full-word forms need native-speaker confirmation
ws2_sanskrit.thin_notes: jala is ambiguous (water primary, net secondary) but valid for network — noted, not rejected; kosh_ksham is thin (ksham = capable, adjective, not capacity, noun kshamata) for a function returning a number — noted, not rejected
